question: For the top-20 sponsors by FY2024 DAF assets, record the default donor-information setting a donor sees when recommending a grant (full contact / name only / fund name only / anonymous), using public help pages, program policies and grant-recommendation tutorials only (no logins). Compare with the DAF Research Collaborative's sponsor survey (36% full contact, 35% fund-name-only default, n=128, 86% community foundations), to test whether the 'partially anonymous by default' problem nonprofits report sits with community foundations or with the national sponsors that send most grants
conclusion_affected: Whether a 'confidential, not anonymous' default or a sponsor data standard (entry option S2) would remove most nonprofit identity complaints; size of the donor-data product gap
rationale: Nonprofit sources rank identity/data problems first (16 of 48 coded findings; 15 of 34 excluding Benevity), but the only default-setting figure is a convenience sample of mostly community foundations. The repo knows Fidelity's 4% anonymous rate, not its default. Public tutorials usually show the default screen

question: Have the owner (a human; ScholarWorks blocks agents in robots.txt and the vendor reports sit behind forms) obtain the DAF Research Collaborative report 'Reinventing the Cycle' (2025, CC BY, IU ScholarWorks) and the FreeWill 2025 and 2026 DAF Report PDFs. Extract the six fundraiser challenges with any frequencies, the source of The NonProfit Times' '79% of DAF gifts are partially anonymous', and FreeWill's sample sizes and question wording for the 72% / 27% / 20% figures
conclusion_affected: How much weight the nonprofit-side anonymity figures can bear (NPS-001, NPS-008, NPS-009), and whether the 79% figure is a misreading
rationale: The NPT 79% 'partially anonymous' headline matches a different DAFRC statistic (79% of occasional partial-anonymity donors feel identifiable), so it may be a misreading. FreeWill figures have no published n. Both are cited in trade press as nonprofit-side facts

question: Census the public, view-only AASP FundSvcs discussion threads that mention DAFs, 2021-2026 (robots.txt allows; no login, no posting). Code each thread by issue category, sponsor or vendor named, and outcome, paraphrasing only and recording no poster names or institutions, to get the first frequency measure of advancement-services complaints by sponsor
conclusion_affected: Whether nonprofit complaints concentrate on intermediaries (Benevity, PPGF) as the complaints corpus suggests, or on national sponsors' data and check practices as the nine AASP threads read here suggest
rationale: Nine threads read here (2022-2026) were the richest first-hand nonprofit source and name Fidelity, Schwab Charitable, Chariot and GiveCampus. The complaints corpus has no such venue (its nonprofit voice is Benevity Trustpilot plus Reddit, which is blocked). Search found at least 17 DAF threads
